div.l: His mouthe as greet / as was a gret furnays Prologꝰus
He was a greet Iangeler / and a golyardeys
And that was most of synne / and harlatrye
Wel cowde he stele corne / and toll thrye
And yet he hadde / a thombe of gold pardye
A white coote / and a blewe hood wered he
A baggepype wel coude he / blowe and sowne
And therwᵗith. al / he browhte vs out of towne
A Ientyl mancyple / was ther of a temple
Off whiche catowrs myght take ensample Mancyple
For to be wys in byggyng of vytayle
For whethir that he payde or toke be tayle
Algate he waytet so / in his acaat
That he was ay be fore and in good astat
Now is that nowht / of god a wol faire grace
That suche a lewde mānnys wyt / shall pace
The wysdam of an heepe / of lernyd men
Of maistres hadde he / mo than thryes ten
That were of lawe / expert and curious
Of whiche ther wer / a doseyn in that house
Worthy to haue stywardys / of Rent and lond
Of any lorde that is in Inglond
To make makemake him lyve / by his propre good
In honowr detteles / but yf he were wood
Or lyve as scarsly / as him lyst desire
And able for to helpyn / al a shire
In any caas / that myht fal or happe
And yet this manciple / set here alder cappe
THe Reve was slender / a coleryk man Reve
His berd was shave / as nyh as ever he can
His herys were be his erys / rownde and shorn
His top was doked like a prest be forn
Wel long were his leggis and wel lene
